boundaries: Only static imports and transparent successful assertion wrappers are transformed. Original callbacks, fixture, delay(6), AbortController and assertions execute in the same realm.
Lexical Response observer forwards finite built-in constructors and returns identical responses; no clone, tee or body consumption.
All reports, progress events, request parsed bodies and exact body text, responses, raw timings and complete formatted lines are retained.

Exact timing values differ across execution clocks. All must be finite/nonnegative; the original disabled-deadline definition additionally requires each measured row latency_ms >= 4 before projection. Native tests must enforce this same predicate on real elapsed time.

Stable digest sets exactly those named fields to zero and regenerates formatting from that projected report. Native formatter must instead match raw captured strings on raw captured reports, without exclusions.

Own-undefined properties are tagged explicitly; native Option omission must not become null. AbortSignal object identity has no Rust drop-in equivalent: Rust library callers supply CancellationToken and retain separate preparation/runtime deadline behavior.

Actual TimeoutError signal identity and non-aborted successful runtime signals are observed. Rust equivalents require real production deadline/drop behavior, not injected timeout responses. Startup uses a separate 60000ms bound even when runtime timeout is zero.
No service/provider/model/download, hardware performance or other-platform qualification. This is a synthetic timer behavior check, not a speed benchmark.
